title: Two Sum
description: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`. You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
hints: A brute force approach would check all pairs in O(n^2) time. Can we do better with auxiliary space?
Can we use a Hash Map to store numbers we have already seen and their indices?
For each element x, check if (target - x) is in the Hash Map. If it is, return both indices.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i-th` day. You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy one stock and choosing a different day in the future to sell that stock.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6), profit = 6-1 = 5.

hints: Keep track of the minimum purchase price seen so far as you iterate through the list.
At each day, calculate profit if sold today: prices[i] - minPrice.
Maintain the maximum profit observed.

title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
description: Given an integer array `nums`, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has the largest sum 6.

hints: Think about resetting the current running sum whenever it drops below zero.
At index i, either add nums[i] to current sum or start fresh from nums[i].
currentSum = max(nums[i], currentSum + nums[i])

title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is equal to the product of all the elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`, without using the division operator in O(n) time.

examples.explanation: Result at 0 is 2*3*4=24, at 1 is 1*3*4=12, etc.

hints: Construct prefix products from left to right.
Multiply with suffix products from right to left.
You can store the left products in the result array and maintain a running suffix product variable.

title: Merge Intervals
description: Given an array of `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [starti, endi]`, merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

examples.explanation: Since [1,3] and [2,6] overlap, merge them into [1,6].

hints: Sort intervals by their starting times first.
Iterate through sorted intervals: if current interval starts before or at the end of the previous interval, merge them by updating the end time.
Otherwise, append current interval to results.

title: Valid Anagram
description: Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, and `false` otherwise.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: Check if lengths match first.
Count character frequencies using an array of size 26 or a hash table.
Increment for string s, decrement for string t; check if all counts are 0.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string `s`, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
hints: Use sliding window technique with two pointers (left and right).
Store the latest index seen for each character in a map.
When a duplicate is encountered, advance left pointer to max(left, lastSeenIndex + 1).

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description: Given a string `s`, return the longest palindromic substring in `s`.
hints: A palindrome mirrors around its center.
Expand around center for all 2N - 1 possible centers (odd length and even length).
Keep track of max start index and max length.

title: Group Anagrams
description: Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.
hints: Two strings are anagrams if and only if their sorted strings are equal.
Use the sorted string or character count tuple as a hash map key.
Collect all matching original words in the corresponding list.

title: Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string `s` containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.
hints: Push opening brackets onto a stack.
When encountering a closing bracket, check if top of stack matches.
At the end, verify if stack is completely empty.

title: Reverse Linked List
description: Given the `head` of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list.
hints: Maintain three pointers: prev, curr, and next.
Save curr.next, point curr.next to prev, then advance prev and curr.
Return prev when curr becomes null.

title: Detect Cycle in Linked List
description: Given `head`, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it using Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm.

examples.explanation: There is a cycle connecting tail to node 1.

hints: Use two pointers: slow moving 1 step, fast moving 2 steps.
If slow and fast ever meet, a cycle exists.
If fast reaches null, no cycle exists.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list by splicing together nodes.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in each list <= 50
hints: Use a dummy node to hold the merged list.
Compare values of current nodes from list1 and list2.
Attach remaining elements at the end.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
description: Given the `head` of a linked list, remove the `nth` node from the end of the list and return its head in one pass.
hints: Advance first pointer n + 1 steps ahead.
Move both pointers together until first reaches the end.
Second pointer will now point just before the node to delete.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return its maximum depth (number of nodes along longest path from root to leaf).
hints: Recursive base case: if root is null, depth is 0.
Return 1 + max(maxDepth(root.left), maxDepth(root.right)).

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST).
hints: Pass valid min and max boundaries down to child subtrees.
For left child, update max to current node val; for right child, update min.
Alternatively perform in-order traversal and verify strictly increasing order.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (i.e., from left to right, level by level).
hints: Use BFS with a Queue.
At each level, note the queue size and process that exact number of nodes.
Collect node values in a sub-array and enqueue child nodes.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
description: Given a binary search tree (BST), find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) node of two given nodes `p` and `q`.
hints: Use BST ordering property.
If both p and q values are smaller than root, LCA is in left subtree.
If both are greater, LCA is in right subtree. Otherwise, current node is the split point (LCA).

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
description: Design an algorithm to serialize a binary tree into a string and deserialize that string back into the original tree structure.

starterCode.javascript:
function serialize(root) {}
function deserialize(data) {}

hints: Use pre-order traversal with delimiter like comma.
Encode null nodes with a sentinel character like "#".
When deserializing, reconstruct recursively reading tokens.

title: Number of Islands
description: Given an `m x n` 2D binary grid `grid` which represents a map of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands.
hints: Iterate through grid cells.
When you find a '1', increment island count and trigger DFS/BFS to mark all connected land as visited ('0').
Check 4-directional bounds.

title: Clone Graph
description: Given a reference of a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy (clone) of the graph.
hints: Use a hash map mapping original nodes to cloned nodes.
Perform DFS or BFS traversal.
For each neighbor, create copy if not seen, and connect to current copy.

title: Course Schedule (Cycle Detection / Topo Sort)
description: There are a total of `numCourses` courses labeled `0` to `numCourses - 1`. Given prerequisites `[a, b]` meaning you must take `b` before `a`, return `true` if you can finish all courses.
hints: Model problem as finding cycle in directed graph using Kahn's Algorithm (indegree BFS).
Compute indegree of all nodes and add 0-indegree nodes to queue.
Count processed nodes: if count equals numCourses, no cycle.

title: Word Ladder
description: Given two words `beginWord` and `endWord`, and a dictionary `wordList`, return the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence from `beginWord` to `endWord`.
hints: Shortest transformation path = BFS on an unweighted graph.
Generate 1-character variations for the current word.
Check existence in word set and track visited words.

title: Climbing Stairs
description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes `n` steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
hints: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2].
Notice this is the Fibonacci sequence.
Optimize space to O(1) by maintaining just two variables.

title: Coin Change
description: You are given an integer array `coins` representing coins of different denominations and an integer `amount`. Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount, or `-1` if impossible.
hints: Initialize dp array of size amount + 1 with infinity.
For each i from 1 to amount, dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i - coin] + 1).

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

examples.explanation: The longest increasing subsequence is [2,3,7,101], therefore the length is 4.

hints: DP approach: dp[i] = max(dp[j] + 1) for all j < i where nums[j] < nums[i].
Patience sorting / Binary search approach runs in O(N log N).
Maintain tails array and use binary search to insert/replace.

title: 0/1 Knapsack Problem
description: Given weights and values of `n` items, put these items in a knapsack of capacity `W` to get the maximum total value in the knapsack.

examples.explanation: Pick items 2 and 3 for weight 50 and value 220.

starterCode.python:
def knap_sack(W, weights, values, n):
    pass

hints: dp[w] represents maximum value with knapsack capacity w.
Iterate items outer loop, capacity w from W down to weights[i] to avoid re-using item in same pass.
dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - weights[i]] + values[i]).

title: Edit Distance
description: Given two strings `word1` and `word2`, return the minimum number of operations required to convert `word1` to `word2` (insert, delete, replace).
hints: dp[i][j] = min operations to transform word1[0..i-1] into word2[0..j-1].
If characters match, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1].
Else, dp[i][j] = 1 + min(insert dp[i][j-1], delete dp[i-1][j], replace dp[i-1][j-1]).

title: Min Stack
description: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time O(1).
hints: Maintain two stacks: a main data stack and a minStack tracking the current minimum at each level.
When pushing x, also push min(x, minStack.top()) to minStack.
Pop both in tandem.

title: Daily Temperatures (Monotonic Stack)
description: Given an array of integers `temperatures`, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is the number of days you have to wait after the `ith` day to get a warmer temperature.
hints: Use a monotonic decreasing stack storing indices.
When encountering a temperature greater than stack top index, pop and calculate days difference: i - prevIndex.
Push current index onto stack.

title: Implement Queue using Stacks
description: Implement a first in first out (FIFO) queue using only two stacks.
hints: Use stackIn for push operations, and stackOut for pop and peek operations.
When stackOut is empty, transfer all elements from stackIn to stackOut (reversing their order to FIFO).

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: You are given an array of integers `nums`, there is a sliding window of size `k` which is moving from the very left to the very right. Return the max sliding window.
hints: Use a double-ended queue (deque) storing indices in decreasing order of values.
Remove indices falling out of the window [i - k + 1, i].
Pop smaller elements from back before inserting new element.

title: Binary Search
description: Given an array of integers `nums` which is sorted in ascending order, and an integer `target`, write a function to search `target` in `nums`. If `target` exists, then return its index. Otherwise, return `-1`.
hints: Initialize low = 0, high = nums.length - 1.
mid = low + Math.floor((high - low) / 2).
Adjust low or high depending on nums[mid] comparison.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Given the sorted array `nums` after rotation at an unknown pivot index, find the index of `target`, or `-1` if not found in O(log n) time.
hints: One half of the array will always be strictly sorted.
Check if left half (nums[low] <= nums[mid]) is sorted.
If sorted and target lies within [nums[low], nums[mid]], search left, otherwise search right.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Given the sorted rotated array `nums` of unique elements, return the minimum element of this array.
hints: Compare nums[mid] with nums[high].
If nums[mid] > nums[high], minimum must be in right half (low = mid + 1).
Else minimum is in left half or is mid (high = mid).

title: Koko Eating Bananas
description: Koko loves to eat bananas. Given `piles` and `h` hours, return the minimum integer `k` such that she can eat all bananas within `h` hours.

examples.explanation: At speed 4 bananas/hr she eats in 8 hours.

hints: Binary search on the answer space: range of speeds is [1, max(piles)].
For candidate speed k, calculate total hours: sum(ceil(p / k)).
If total hours <= h, try smaller speed (high = mid); else increase speed (low = mid + 1).

title: Jump Game
description: You are given an integer array `nums`. You are initially positioned at the array's first index, and each element in the array represents your maximum jump length at that position. Return `true` if you can reach the last index, or `false` otherwise.

examples.explanation: Jump 1 step from index 0 to 1, then 3 steps to the last index.

hints: Maintain the furthest reachable index `maxReach`.
At index i, if i > maxReach, return false.
Update maxReach = max(maxReach, i + nums[i]). If maxReach >= nums.length - 1, return true.

title: Gas Station
description: There are `n` gas stations along a circular route, where the amount of gas at the `ith` station is `gas[i]`. You have a car with an unlimited gas tank and it costs `cost[i]` of gas to travel from the `ith` station to its next `(i + 1)th` station. Return the starting gas station's index if you can travel around the circuit once in the clockwise direction, otherwise return `-1`.
hints: If total sum of gas < total sum of cost, completing the circuit is impossible (return -1).
Maintain tank = 0. Iterate stations: tank += gas[i] - cost[i].
If tank < 0, reset tank to 0 and set start = i + 1.

title: Task Scheduler
description: Given a characters array `tasks`, representing the tasks a CPU needs to do, where each letter represents a different task. Tasks could be done in any order. Each task is done in one unit of time. For each unit of time, the CPU could complete either one task or just be idle. However, there is a non-negative integer `n` that represents the cooldown period between two same tasks. Return the least number of units of times that the CPU will take to finish all the given tasks.

examples.explanation: A -> B -> idle -> A -> B -> idle -> A -> B.

hints: Find the task with maximum frequency `maxFreq`.
Count how many tasks share this maximum frequency `maxCount`.
Formula: max(tasks.length, (maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1) + maxCount).

title: Assign Cookies
description: Assume you are an awesome parent and want to give your children some cookies. Each child `i` has a greed factor `g[i]`, and each cookie `j` has a size `s[j]`. Maximize the number of satisfied children.

examples.explanation: Only child with greed 1 can be satisfied.

hints: Sort both greed array `g` and cookie size array `s`.
Greedily satisfy the child with the smallest greed using the smallest possible cookie that suffices.
Iterate with two pointers.
timeComplexity: O(N log N + M log M)
